text:
mira: Seeing a hard p99 spike for a Dedicated customer (pool-c). Customer reported timeouts and 10-20x p99 increase after a traffic burst. Metrics: p95 ~ 350ms -> 420ms, p99 jumped 2.8s -> 9.6s. Affected routes: /v1/generate (large context).

sam: Can you paste the allocator/attach logs? Any recent image changes or kernel updates? :eyes:

mira: quick logs from attach controller:
```
I0317 14:12:10 attach_controller.go:214] attach request for pool-c instance-332 queued
I0317 14:12:14 dockerd: Pulling image "redwood/runtime:v3.2.1"
E0317 14:12:45 kubelet: ImagePullBackOff: Back-off pulling image
I0317 14:12:50 attach_controller.go:332] cold-start latency 36s (image pull dominated)
```

tony: that ImagePullBackOff is suspicious — we saw a registry blip earlier in eu-west. Could be concurrent hotattach causing thundering herd and registry rate limiting. Two mitigations: increase min_pool for pool-c (temporary) and enable image pre-pull on warm nodes.

lucy: customer impact note: they hit 503s and timed out, ticket escalated to Tier2. They need a status update ASAP. Proposed immediate actions below. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Escalation created: INC-2026-331. Notifying account team.

mira: quick repro steps from our load test: ramp 200 concurrent requests with long context (~8k tokens) targeting pool-c. Observed attach queue length spike and many requests waiting for cold GPUs.

sam: timeline looks like: heavy ramp -> autoscaler attempted to spin new instances -> image pulls queued -> registry throttling -> attach queue growth -> p99 spike. Also noticed model cache warmup delayed (KV cache miss) which increased token time.

tony: short-term playbook: 1) bump min_pool for pool-c to +3 GPUs 2) activate fallback routing to smaller quantized model for that customer 3) short TTL prepull for next 10min 4) throttle new concurrent sessions for that API key

lucy: i'll draft the customer note. If we do fallback routing, we should keep a canary to compare quality.

mira: command to bump min_pool (internal cli):
```bash
redwoodctl pools update pool-c --min-instances 6 --burst-capacity 2
```

tony: i'll run the CLI after approval. Also rolling a small runtime tweak to reduce image size for v3.2.1 is in progress (should cut pull time ~40%). deploy-bot: any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deployment event: runtime-service v3.2.1 rolled to eu-west at 2026-03-17T14:05:12Z (sha: a1b2c3). No runtime rollbacks.

sam: secondary mitigation: enable prefix/KV caching warmups for active customer prompts and pin their requests to warm nodes via sticky routing. That will reduce downstream token latency while we mitigate image pulls.

mira: for immediate customer relief i propose: - bump min_pool now - enable fallback to smaller model - apply rate limit to API key (graceful 429 gating) - run image pre-pull job on 3 warm nodes

lucy: agreed. i'll send the customer an ETA ~30min and note mitigations.

tony: doing the pool bump and pre-pull now. I'll post back when done.

(2 minutes later)
ton y: pool update complete. Pre-pull job kicked off to 3 nodes.

mira: rerunning load test — attach median back ~420ms, p99 reduced to ~1.2s (improved but not baseline). Customer reported degraded but usable.

sam: follow-ups: 1) add registry retry/backoff for concurrent pulls 2) optimize runtime image layering to reduce cold pulls 3) tune autoscaler backoff window to avoid spike provisioning 4) automated pre-warm for priority customers.

lucy: assigned owners: tony -> pool + infra fixes, sam -> autoscaler tuning + cache warmups, mira -> customer comms + short-term routing. I'll file a post-incident doc.

mira: quick notes to add to post-incident: observed root cause = registry throttling + cold GPU attach + large-context KV misses. Mitigations executed = min_pool bump, pre-pull, fallback model routing, API key soft throttling. Next steps = image optimizations, autoscaler cooldown tuning, proactive prewarm for SLAs.

support-bot: INC-2026-331 updated with mitigations and assignees.

sam: thanks team. let's reconvene EOD to validate the runtime image change and confirm long-term config. :checkered_flag:
